data.narrative:
Black Forest Labs, a Series B AI & Software company, is evaluated against a peer set of five same-sector comparables spanning Series A through Series C, supplemented by nine private and one public reference (Palantir). The company's last post-money valuation stands at $3.25B against $450M total raised.

Two triangulation methods yield convergent but distinct signals. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implying $6.2B. Peer-median analysis across five AI & Software companies—including Figure AI ($39.0B, Series C), Reflection AI ($25.0B, Series A), Skild AI ($14.0B, Series C), Together AI ($8.3B, Series A), and Physical Intelligence ($5.6B, Series B)—yields a $14.0B median, with range spanning $5.6B to $39.0B. The median approach is weighted by the relevance of stage-adjacent comparables but reflects the sector's wide valuation dispersion.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $5.2B to $16.1B, with a median of $10.1B. The current $3.25B valuation sits materially below both derived ranges, reflecting typical early-stage discounting. Key uncertainties include the heterogeneity of peer stage dynamics within frontier AI—Series A multiples here approach Series C levels elsewhere—and limited public market anchoring. Stage progression toward Series C, revenue traction, and competitive positioning relative to Physical Intelligence (nearest stage peer) represent primary drivers of range realization.
